topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students, connects the session to recent histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classifications, mechanisms, and mutational genetics of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes and illustrate how their mutations disrupt cell cycle regulation and cellular phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and forms of genetic instability in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary predispositions, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cumulative genetic alterations drive cancer progression, how inherited mutations accelerate this process, and how tumors evolve during treatment.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation, invites questions, and recommends supplementary reading for the upcoming break.
